question: Should existing injected WhatsApp media readers without explicit local roots intentionally fail after this upgrade, or receive a temporary guarded compatibility path?
rationale: The stricter boundary closes an observable local-file access widening, but it can stop existing integrations at runtime; repository policy requires explicit ownership of that security-versus-upgrade choice.

options.title: Keep the fail-closed boundary
options.body: Require explicit local roots, preserve the canonical runtime re-export, and add a clear upgrade diagnostic and focused compatibility coverage.

options.title: Add temporary guarded compatibility
options.body: Preserve legacy injected readers only through a narrowly documented deprecation path with a removal plan and tests that prevent unrestricted root widening.

recommendation.title: Keep the fail-closed boundary
recommendation.body: Require explicit local roots, preserve the canonical runtime re-export, and add a clear upgrade diagnostic and focused compatibility coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Their prior merged WhatsApp runtime and canonical-media work makes them the closest available owner of this exact boundary.
